title: Japan Specified Skilled Worker Visa 2026: SSW Guide
metaDescription: Japan Specified Skilled Worker visa 2026: 19 sectors, JLPT N4 language rule, SSW-1 and SSW-2 differences, tests and how to apply from abroad.
headline: Japan Specified Skilled Worker Visa 2026: Full Guide

sections.title: What the SSW visa is
sections.content:
The Specified Skilled Worker (SSW) status was created in April 2019 to bring foreign workers into Japanese sectors short of staff, and it requires no university degree. As of November 2026 it covers 19 sectors, after new fields such as logistics warehouses, linen supply and resource recycling were added, alongside the original sectors of nursing care, construction, agriculture, food service and manufacturing.

The government raised the overall cap to 820,000 SSW workers over the five years from 2024 to 2029, more than double the previous target. At the end of June 2026 there were 444,256 SSW workers in Japan, with about 233,000 changing status inside Japan and about 211,000 entering from abroad.

sections.title: SSW-1 versus SSW-2
sections.content:
SSW-1 is the entry level. You can work in Japan for up to five years in total, not five years per employer, and you cannot bring family members as dependants. It suits workers starting out in a sector, and most applicants enter through this route.

SSW-2 is the advanced level, with no time limit, renewable indefinitely, and it allows you to bring your spouse and children as dependants. It is available in most sectors except nursing care, where workers seeking a path to indefinite stay use the dedicated Care Worker residence status instead. Upgrading to SSW-2 needs higher skills and Japanese ability.

sections.title: Requirements: language and skills tests
sections.content:
SSW-1 has three core requirements: you must be 18 or older, pass the sector skills test, and pass a Japanese test. The language test is JLPT N4 or higher, or the Japan Foundation Test for Basic Japanese (JFT-Basic). Taxi and bus drivers and railway staff need N3 level, and nursing care adds its own Japanese test.

The skills test is set by the relevant ministry or industry association for each sector and is offered both inside Japan and in sending countries, often through Prometric. Workers who completed Technical Intern Training (ii) in a related field for at least two years are typically exempt from both the language and skills tests.

sections.title: How to apply and stay safe
sections.content:
Find a legitimate employer in your sector, pass both tests, and have the employer apply for your Certificate of Eligibility through the Immigration Services Agency. The standard application fee for a Certificate of Eligibility or status change is ¥6,000 at the counter or ¥5,500 online, a fee introduced in mid-2025.

Your sector, job category and the work assigned must all match, so never accept a job in a different sector from the test you passed. Use only the official SSW support website and your country's licensed agencies, and beware of agents who promise a visa without tests or demand large upfront fees.

faqs.q: What is the Japan SSW visa?
faqs.a: The Specified Skilled Worker visa is Japan's work status for foreign nationals in sectors short of staff, created in April 2019. It needs no university degree, covers 19 sectors as of November 2026, and has two levels: SSW-1 for up to five years, and SSW-2 with no time limit and family dependants allowed.

faqs.q: What Japanese level do I need for the SSW visa?
faqs.a: You need JLPT N4 or higher, or the JFT-Basic test, which covers basic daily conversation and simple sentences. Taxi and bus drivers and railway transport staff need N3 level. Workers who completed Technical Intern Training (ii) in good standing in a related field are usually exempt from the language test.

faqs.q: Which sectors can I work in under SSW?
faqs.a: The SSW programme covers 19 sectors in 2026, including nursing care, building cleaning, construction, agriculture, food service, manufacturing, shipbuilding, automobile repair, aviation, accommodation, automobile transportation, railway, logistics warehouses, linen supply and resource recycling. SSW-2 is available in most sectors except nursing care.

faqs.q: Can I bring my family on the SSW visa?
faqs.a: Not on SSW-1, which allows a stay of up to five years in total and no dependants. On SSW-2, which has no time limit and is renewable indefinitely, you can bring your spouse and children as dependants. Upgrading from SSW-1 to SSW-2 requires higher skills and Japanese ability plus passing the relevant examinations.
